summary: Rate-controller epoch swap triggering staggered 429s for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Nimbus Analytics reported sudden waves of 429 responses across multiple API keys after a scheduled configuration change to the dedicated pool's rate-controller epoch boundary. The pattern is 'staggered' — different worker hosts start rejecting at slightly different times over a ~3 minute window, causing partial throughput degradation rather than a single outage.

Impact:
- ~20% of requests for the tenant returned 429 intermittently for 15–40 minutes during the window.
- Affected traffic is primarily short chat requests and small-batch embeddings.
- Customer's ingest backlog increased (ingest latency SLA breached for several jobs).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (tenant-dedicated-893) in prod-us-west (us-west-2).
- Rate-controller version: v2.3.7 (control-plane) / runtime v1.9.2.
- Autoscaler and health probe config recently adjusted (epoch boundary tweak deployed 2026-03-10 01:40 UTC).

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Run 250 parallel short chat requests (latency target 100–300ms) across 8 worker hosts pinned to tenant-dedicated-893.
2) Simultaneously trigger a config push that rotates the rate-controller epoch boundary (test toggle used by SRE to shift refill windows).
3) Observe that 2–3 hosts begin returning 429s within 30–90s, others follow over ~3 minutes.

Logs / telemetry pointers:
- Trace IDs from customer: trace-20260310-nimbus-01 (sampled traces attached).
- Rate-limiter metrics: token_refill_latency spike aligned with epoch swap (see grafana panel /d/rate-limiter/epoch-swap).
- Autoscaler logs: small flurry of readiness toggles across hosts during swap (k8s events linked).

Additional context:
Customer reports this is a new behavior since a control-plane optimization was turned on to reduce cross-host refill jitter. They only began seeing customer-visible 429s after this change and request advice on safe configuration limits and immediate mitigations.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:12 - Maya Chen (Support): Initial triage completed with customer. Collected traces and load pattern. Escalated to SRE for rate-limiter investigation.

2026-03-10 09:05 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Confirmed epoch boundary change at 2026-03-10T01:40Z in control plane. Observed token_refill_latency burst and token_bucket_saturation on 3 hosts. Attaching metric snapshots.
2026-03-10 10:20 - Lina Gómez (Customer Success): Customer is concerned about ingest SLA breach; requested temporary mitigation (disable epoch-swap feature or increase burst credits).

2026-03-11 02:30 - Arjun Patel (SRE): Rolled out temporary mitigation: disabled epoch-sync optimization for tenant-dedicated-893 and applied a conservative burst allowance for priority lanes. Initial customer report: errors reduced but still saw small tail of 429s for ~20 minutes.

2026-03-12 15:40 - Eng (Rate Limiter team): Creating follow-up change to make epoch transitions atomic per-tenant and introduce a 60s overlap window to avoid staggered refills. ETA for canary: 2026-03-14.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Epoch boundary rotation causes non-atomic refill state; hosts that apply boundary at different millisecond offsets experience token starvation briefly leading to 429s.
Hypothesis 2: Dedicated pool autoscaler readiness toggles briefly drop health checks which combine with reduced burst credits to trigger 429s as queued requests attempt to retry simultaneously.
Observed: metric token_refill_latency correlates with start of 429 waves. Host-by-host timelines show up to 180s skew between first and last host reporting saturation.
Checked: no tenant-wide quota change or billing event at time of incident. No model fallback activity observed. No CPU/GPU exhaustion on serving hosts.

Dashboards: /d/rate-limiter/epoch-swap -> shows refill histogram; /d/autoscaler/host-readiness -> shows readiness toggles at same time. Logs: k8s readiness probe flaps due to config reload ordering (link to logs).
resolution_notes: Workaround applied (2026-03-11 02:30): reverted epoch-sync optimization for tenant-dedicated-893 and increased temporary burst allowance for priority lanes. This reduced error rate from ~20% to <2% during subsequent test windows.

Permanent fix plan: implement atomic epoch-swap mechanism in rate-controller (engineering PR opened) + add a 60s overlap period where both old and new refill windows are honored to avoid starvation. Also add conservative jitter to control-plane pushes to avoid simultaneous host restarts.
Rollout plan: canary change to 10% of dedicated pools on 2026-03-14, monitor token_refill_latency and tenant 429 rate for 48 hours. Full rollout after safety verification.
Follow-ups: update Dedicated Pool runbook with guidance on safe epoch-boundary changes and add console warning when toggling epoch-sync optimizations that affect refill timing.
Owner: Arjun Patel (SRE) for mitigations and rollout. Engineering PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/523 (linked).
